name: Kotlin notes service
description: A Kotlin service with SQL built by string interpolation, a shell command, MD5, java.util.Random tokens, ObjectInputStream and a hard-coded password. Intentionally insecure, for education.
expected: Findings from the JVM token scanner (Java/Kotlin rules).

fixes.title: Read the password from the environment
fixes.explanation: The password is no longer in the repository (rotate the exposed value).

fixes.title: Use a PreparedStatement
fixes.explanation: The term is bound as a parameter instead of being interpolated into the SQL text.
edits:
val stmt = conn.createStatement()
    val rs = stmt.executeQuery("SELECT * FROM notes WHERE title LIKE '%$term%'")

val stmt = conn.prepareStatement("SELECT * FROM notes WHERE title LIKE ?")
    stmt.setString(1, "%$term%")
    val rs = stmt.executeQuery()

fixes.title: Run ls with an argument list
fixes.explanation: No shell parses the directory name; it is one argument to a fixed program.

fixes.title: Use SHA-256 instead of MD5
fixes.explanation: MD5 is broken for security use.

fixes.title: Use SecureRandom for the token
fixes.explanation: SecureRandom is a cryptographically secure source.

fixes.title: Do not deserialize untrusted bytes
fixes.explanation: The bytes are treated as text data instead of being turned back into objects.
